why_the_lane_exists: a SUPPORT verdict is the least examined outcome in the mesh. When one reviewing lens supports a row instead of challenging it, that row receives less adversarial attention than any challenged row, and agreement can be agreement about the wrong thing. The B-8 lane audits those rows as shipped with a deliberately adversarial reading and reports the defect rate as a digit whatever it turns out to be.

frame_and_sample.frame_rule: rows the LF lens verdicted support, retired rows dropped, id-sorted

headline_digit.reading: every sampled supported row carried at least one defect, and six of seven carried a medium. The lane's hypothesis is confirmed for this book: a support verdict did not mean the row was sound, it meant the row had not been pressed.

findings.character: evidence and warrant defects, not boundary errors: unswept or overstated universals, a form-class equation that does not hold, a recurrence claimed at the wrong tier, gloss extent exceeding its splice, a compound signal key mixing two device classes, a seam argued as decided where its partner discloses it as held, and a mark citation missing its single-witness caveat.

campaign_significance: this is the strongest single argument in the campaign for keeping the B-8 lane on every book. The deterministic suite was hard-GREEN over these rows with zero triage flags, and two earlier repair waves had already rewritten them. None of that surfaced these twelve defects; an adversarial read of the least-challenged rows did.
disposition: all twelve ordered to the micro cure round; none requires a boundary change
